doc.title: Terry Gibbs interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 12, 2001 [interview 1 of 2]

title: Audio interlude: Allen's All Stars at Joe Pasternak's house
summary: Gibbs hears an old live party recording with Steve Allen and explains how it came about.

story.theme_name: Radio and television work: staff jobs, shows and broadcasts
story.community_name: Working with Sinatra: bands, Vegas and the Sands

blocks.x: Let me play something for you.
Oh God it’ll probably be terrible. I hate things I did in the past.
Is that Gus Bivona and myself? At Joe Pasternak’s house.
That’s right. That’s right. I have this— you know who that was?

I was wild. Pete Rugolo, who was then the A&R person, the producer was called the artists and repertoire man. He was the producer. And I wanted to do a live date. Because Steve and I became very good friends. And the fact that he was living in New York, and he bought a home in California, and every time he’d come to visit his children he’d give me a call and — it was empty, the house. And I’d call and we’d jam. And I got bummed, when Jayne moved out here they made a house out of it, and took away our jam session house. They put furniture in and ruined the whole house. So when Steve came out one time I said, “Let’s do something.” So I told Pete Rugolo, we used to do live dates at a party, and Pete was in with all the Hollywood crowd. And I don’t think many of the young people or older people may not remember the name Joe Pasternak. He was the biggest producer of musicals. Judy Garland and Mickey Rooney. All those musicals he produced. So we did it at his house. And he loved it. We did it as out and out fun.
You know I hate to listen to old things I did. Oh I don’t hate to, but what’s good about listening to them, I remember that time. What was going on in my life at that time. It was a fun time.
